chapter.title: Design principles
chapter.para: The requirements in the following chapters follow from these principles.

varlistentry.term: One root for the operating system

listitem.para: Everything the operating system ships or installs lives under /overlayer. The root directory holds only that directory, user data and the virtual filesystems the kernel provides.
The base layer is changed only by base upgrades, the userland layer only by the package manager, the boot layer only by base upgrades and the installer. No layer writes into another.

varlistentry.term: The base stands on its own

listitem.para: The base layer is a complete, bootable system. Deleting the userland layer leaves a working system, never a broken one.
Layers are combined into one view by stacking them (OverlayFS), not by copying files of one layer into another. Each file on disk belongs to exactly one layer.

varlistentry.term: Each C library in its own directory

listitem.para: A C library, its loader, its headers and its toolchain live together in a directory named after the library's target triplet. Two C libraries never share a lib or include directory.

varlistentry.term: No compatibility directories at the root

listitem.para: There is no /usr, /lib64 or /bin, not even as a symbolic link. Software that names those paths is served by path resolution at run time instead.
A new base is prepared while the system runs and put in place at the next boot, before anything uses it. The running system never sees a half-upgraded base.
